original_question: Do there exist classical knots that are not slice in the ordinary classical sense but become slice either in Kauffman's notion of virtual-knot sliceness or in Turaev's notion of sliceness for knots in thickened surfaces, and if a knot in a thickened surface is slice in Turaev's sense, must it stabilize to a virtual knot that is slice in Kauffman's sense?
target_in_paper: Section 8.2.4, "Questions from Micah W. Chrisman," items 1–2. The paper states this as a two-part open problem about whether ordinary classical sliceness is detected by Kauffman’s virtual-knot sliceness or by Turaev’s sliceness for knots in thickened surfaces, and whether Turaev-sliceness implies Kauffman-sliceness after stabilization. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))
correct_elements: Your draft already tracks the paper very closely: it captures both numbered questions in §8.2.4, correctly distinguishes the three sliceness notions involved (classical, Kauffman, Turaev), and correctly includes the second stabilization question relating Turaev’s and Kauffman’s frameworks. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))
missing_details: The paper is asking about knots, not links, and the Kauffman-side definitions are given for oriented knots or links; to make the question stand-alone, one should specify the single-component oriented setting. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

The phrase "slice in Kauffman’s sense" should be unpacked using Definition 8.1: a virtual knot is slice if it is virtually concordant to the unknot, equivalently to the empty knot, by a genus-zero virtual cobordism built from virtual isotopies, births, deaths, and oriented saddle moves. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

The meaning of "stabilize" is implicit in §2.3: virtual knots are identified with stable equivalence classes of knots in thickened surfaces, where stable equivalence means isotopy in the thickened surfaces, homeomorphisms of the surfaces, and addition or subtraction of empty handles. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

The paper records a known one-way implication before posing the question: a knot in R^2 × R that is slice in the classical sense is slice in both Turaev’s and Kauffman’s senses. The open problem is whether either converse can fail. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

To be fully stand-alone, "classically slice" should be stated in the ordinary classical sense for a classical knot K in R^3 ≅ R^2 × R, namely as the usual sliceness notion from classical knot concordance. The paper uses this phrase without re-defining it in §8.2.4. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

No algebraic data such as a coefficient ring, field, variables, degree conditions, homogeneity, nilpotency, or quantifiers like "for all sufficiently large m" are relevant here; the incompleteness is entirely in the topological definitions and the precise stabilization/concordance language. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))
refined_question: Does the converse to the implication recorded in §8.2.4 hold? Precisely: let K be a classical oriented knot in R^3 ≅ R^2 × R. Must K be classically slice whenever, viewed as a virtual knot, it is slice in Kauffman’s sense (that is, virtually concordant to the unknot, equivalently to the empty knot, by a genus-zero cobordism generated by virtual isotopies, births, deaths, and oriented saddle moves), or whenever, viewed as a knot in a thickened surface, it is slice in Turaev’s sense? Moreover, if a knot in a thickened surface is slice in Turaev’s sense, must its stable-equivalence class under isotopy, surface homeomorphism, and addition/removal of empty handles contain a virtual knot that is slice in Kauffman’s sense? ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))
equivalent_formulation: On the Kauffman side, one may equivalently replace "virtually concordant to the unknot" by "virtually concordant to the empty knot," since Definition 8.1 states these are equivalent. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))
justification: This draft does not target Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3; it instead matches §8.2.4 almost verbatim, specifically the two questions attributed there to Micah W. Chrisman. The nearby context needed to make the question self-contained comes from §8.2, Definition 8.1, which defines Kauffman-style virtual cobordism/concordance/sliceness, and from §2.3 together with Theorem 2.1, which explains stable equivalence of knots in thickened surfaces and hence the paper’s use of "stabilize." The citation to Turaev’s framework is reference [227], "Cobordism of knots on surfaces." ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))
